description: Comprehensive bug review across frontend (React/TypeScript), backend (Python/FastAPI), and Rust (Tauri audio system). Identified via static analysis of source code.

bugs.name: conn.total_changes AttributeError on aiosqlite
bugs.description: aiosqlite connections do not have a total_changes attribute (only synchronous sqlite3.Connection does). Will raise AttributeError at runtime when create_process() or save_transcript() is called. Should use cursor.rowcount instead, which is already used correctly elsewhere in the codebase.
bugs.fix: Replace conn.total_changes with cursor.rowcount after the execute() call
bugs.fix_notes: Verified 2026-02-25: all instances now use cursor.rowcount correctly. No references to total_changes remain.

bugs.name: Dual recording state flags can diverge
bugs.description: Two independent AtomicBool flags track recording state: RECORDING_FLAG in lib.rs (line 66) and IS_RECORDING in recording_commands.rs (line 39). start_recording checks one flag then sets the other after success. If recording init partially fails between those two points, the flags diverge permanently. UI thinks recording is active while backend is idle (or vice versa). Only recovery is app restart.
bugs.fix: Remove static IS_RECORDING and always derive from RECORDING_MANAGER.as_ref().map(|m| m.is_recording()).unwrap_or(false)
bugs.fix_notes: Verified 2026-02-25: partially mitigated — frontend now polls backend state every 500ms via syncWithBackend(), reducing user-visible impact. But dual flags (IS_RECORDING AtomicBool + RecordingState.is_recording) still exist and can diverge on partial init failure.

bugs.name: Unsafe static mut data race in pipeline.rs
bugs.description: SAMPLE_COUNTER is a non-atomic u64 mutated from multiple audio threads (mic + system capture) with no synchronization. This is undefined behavior per Rust semantics. Two threads can read/write simultaneously causing lost updates, torn reads, or compiler-optimized incorrect results.
bugs.fix: Replace with static SAMPLE_COUNTER: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0) and use .fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)
bugs.fix_notes: Verified 2026-02-25: now uses AtomicU64 with Ordering::Relaxed. No unsafe static mut remains in active code.

bugs.name: Blocking synchronous sqlite3 in async functions
bugs.description: save_meeting() and save_meeting_transcript() are declared async but use synchronous sqlite3.connect() instead of aiosqlite.connect(). This blocks the event loop, defeating the purpose of async code and causing performance degradation under load.
bugs.fix: Replace sqlite3.connect() with async with aiosqlite.connect() and await all execute calls
bugs.fix_notes: Verified 2026-03-10: Both save_meeting() and save_meeting_transcript() now use async with self._get_connection() as conn with await statements. No synchronous sqlite3.connect() calls remain.

bugs.name: Missing asyncio import causes NameError
bugs.description: main.py uses asyncio.CancelledError (line 689) but never imports asyncio. Will crash with NameError at runtime when an SSE connection is cancelled by the client.
bugs.fix: Add 'import asyncio' to the imports at the top of main.py
bugs.fix_notes: Verified 2026-03-10: asyncio is imported at line 6 of main.py.

bugs.name: asyncio.create_task() in synchronous cleanup method
bugs.description: The cleanup() method in transcript_processor.py is synchronous (not async) but calls asyncio.create_task() which requires a running event loop. Will fail with RuntimeError. Additionally the task is never awaited so Ollama clients are never properly closed.
bugs.fix: Make cleanup() async or use loop.run_until_complete(), or call synchronous close methods instead
bugs.fix_notes: Fixed 2026-03-10: Made cleanup() async, replaced fire-and-forget create_task with direct await asyncio.gather(). Updated callers in main.py (SummaryProcessor.cleanup and lifespan) to await.

bugs.name: Mutex poisoning from .unwrap() on all lock calls
bugs.description: RecordingState has 20+ .lock().unwrap() calls. If any thread panics while holding a mutex lock, the mutex becomes poisoned and ALL subsequent lock attempts will panic. This is especially dangerous in the error callback path (line 312-315) where a panicking callback poisons the error_callback mutex, preventing all future error recovery.
bugs.fix: Replace .lock().unwrap() with .lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) to recover from poisoned mutexes, or use parking_lot::Mutex which never poisons

bugs.name: Progress task infinite loop with no exit condition
bugs.description: The progress_task spawned at line 571 runs an infinite loop emitting events every 500ms. Only cancelled via .abort() after the transcription timeout. If transcription completes quickly, the progress task keeps running until the full timeout. Can emit stale events for 10+ minutes.
bugs.fix: Add a cancellation token (e.g., tokio CancellationToken or watch channel) that is triggered when transcription completes, replacing the infinite loop

bugs.name: Unstable useEffect dependency causes listener thrashing
bugs.description: The useEffect at line 58 depends on handleRecordingStop which is not memoized. This causes the Tauri event listener to be torn down and re-created on every render, potentially missing events during the teardown gap.
bugs.fix: Memoize handleRecordingStop with useCallback, or use a ref to hold the latest function and keep a stable listener
bugs.fix_notes: Verified 2026-03-10: handleRecordingStop is now properly memoized via useCallback in the useRecordingStop hook with correct dependency array.

bugs.name: Event listener cleanup race condition in layout.tsx
bugs.description: Uses .then(fn => fn()) pattern for Tauri unlisten cleanup. The cleanup function can execute before the listener promise resolves, meaning the listener is never unsubscribed and leaks memory.
bugs.fix: Store the unlisten promise and handle cleanup properly using an abort flag pattern or useRef

bugs.name: Dynamic SQL column names via f-strings
bugs.description: Column names are interpolated directly into SQL queries using f-strings in save_api_key, save_transcript_api_key, and related methods. Currently validated against a whitelist, but the pattern is fragile. Any future change that bypasses or extends the whitelist opens a SQL injection vulnerability.
bugs.fix: Use a mapping dict from validated provider names to fixed SQL statements, or use separate methods per provider

bugs.name: Async listener setup race in RecordingStateContext
bugs.description: setupListeners() is async but not awaited. If the component unmounts before listeners are set up, the cleanup function runs but unsubscribers array is incomplete, leaking event listeners.
bugs.fix: Use an abort flag: set a cancelled boolean in cleanup, check it inside setupListeners before registering each listener

bugs.name: Stale closure in setStatus callback
bugs.description: setStatus useCallback depends on state.status, state.isRecording, state.isPaused, causing a new callback reference on every state change. This triggers unnecessary re-renders in all consumers and creates timing windows where the callback captures stale values.
bugs.fix: Use a ref for logging the previous status instead of depending on state values in the callback

bugs.name: Unnecessary router dependency in useRecordingStop
bugs.description: The useEffect has [router] as dependency, but useRouter() can return a new reference on re-renders. This causes the Tauri event listener to be unregistered and re-registered unnecessarily.
bugs.fix: Use a routerRef pattern: store router in a ref and remove from dependency array

bugs.name: Async cleanup race in ConfigContext
bugs.description: Cleanup variable is set via .then() callback but may still be undefined when component unmounts before setup completes. The cleanup function runs, finds undefined, and the event listener leaks.
bugs.fix: Use an abort flag checked inside the async setup, and store unlisten functions in a ref

bugs.name: Missing recordingState dependency in TranscriptContext useEffect
bugs.description: useEffect at line 178 depends on [currentMeetingId] but uses recordingState.isRecording inside the sync logic. When recording state changes, the effect does not re-run, causing stale sync behavior.
bugs.fix: Add recordingState.isRecording to the dependency array

bugs.name: Dangling event listeners from rapid start calls
bugs.description: Two rapid start_recording calls without an intervening stop_recording will overwrite TRANSCRIPT_LISTENER_ID with the second listener ID, leaking the first. The first listener continues receiving transcript-update events and storing transcripts, causing memory bloat.
bugs.fix: Check for and unlisten any existing listener before setting a new one in start_recording

bugs.name: Transcript listener cleaned before manager, losing final transcripts
bugs.description: The transcript event listener is unregistered at line 540-548, but the recording manager (which may still emit transcript events during flush) is not cleaned up until line 819. Transcripts emitted during the 270+ lines of shutdown code between those points are dropped.
bugs.fix: Move listener cleanup to after manager cleanup, or collect transcripts via a channel instead of events during shutdown

bugs.name: IS_RECORDING flag updated too late during stop
bugs.description: IS_RECORDING is set to false at line 854, after 600+ lines of cleanup including transcription wait, model unload, and analytics. During this time, commands like pause_recording and get_recording_state see IS_RECORDING=true but the manager may already be released, risking crashes.
bugs.fix: Set IS_RECORDING to false early (after stopping streams) and use a separate CLEANUP_IN_PROGRESS flag to prevent new operations

bugs.name: Pause duration race condition
bugs.description: In resume_recording(), the lock on pause_start is released after .take(), then a separate lock on total_pause_duration is acquired. Between these two locks, another thread can call pause/resume, potentially calculating the same pause_start twice and corrupting the total pause duration.
bugs.fix: Use a single mutex protecting both pause_start and total_pause_duration, or use a combined struct under one lock

bugs.name: Recording manager held too long during shutdown
bugs.description: The recording manager is moved out of the global static at line 512 but kept alive until line 827 (600+ lines of async operations including API calls and model unloading). During this time it holds file handles, audio buffers, and Arc-based resources unnecessarily.
bugs.fix: Drop the manager immediately after save_recording_only completes, before starting model unload and analytics

bugs.name: Race condition in concurrent process creation
bugs.description: create_process() uses a non-atomic read-then-write pattern (UPDATE then INSERT if 0 rows). Two concurrent requests for the same meeting_id can both see 0 rows from UPDATE, then both attempt INSERT, causing a PRIMARY KEY constraint violation.
bugs.fix: Use INSERT OR REPLACE (upsert) or add a unique constraint with conflict handling

bugs.name: JSONResponse vs HTTPException inconsistency in get_summary
bugs.description: The get_summary() endpoint uses JSONResponse directly for error responses (404, 400, 500) instead of raising HTTPException. This bypasses FastAPI's automatic error handling and response model validation, creating an inconsistent API contract.
bugs.fix: Replace JSONResponse error returns with raise HTTPException(status_code=..., detail=...)

bugs.name: Generic exception masking in API key methods
bugs.description: save_api_key() and save_transcript_api_key() catch all exceptions with 'except Exception', masking validation errors (ValueError from whitelist check) with generic 500 responses instead of returning 400 Bad Request.
bugs.fix: Catch ValueError separately and re-raise as HTTPException(status_code=400) before the generic except block

bugs.name: Stale sendMessageRef in ClaudePanel
bugs.description: sendMessageRef is created but sendMessage function is in the dependency array of a useEffect. The ref and the dependency array disagree about the sendMessage lifecycle, risking calls to a stale function reference.
bugs.fix: Keep sendMessage in ref only and remove from useEffect dependency array, or remove the ref and use the dependency array properly

bugs.name: Global Faker seed affects all instances
bugs.description: Faker.seed() is a class method that seeds ALL Faker instances globally. If multiple meetings are processed concurrently, they share the same seed state, producing non-deterministic surrogates.
bugs.fix: Create a per-instance Faker with its own random.Random seed instead of using the global class method

bugs.name: Empty string vs None ambiguity in get_api_key
bugs.description: get_api_key() returns empty string '' when no key is found, but callers may not distinguish this from a valid empty key. Some callers may expect None for missing keys.
bugs.fix: Return None for missing keys and update callers to handle Optional[str]

bugs.name: Manual ref synchronization pattern in ScreenshotContext
bugs.description: Ref is kept in sync with state manually, which is error-prone. If a developer adds a new state update path without updating the ref, they silently diverge.
bugs.fix: Use a custom hook that automatically syncs ref with state, or restructure to avoid needing both

bugs.name: Misleading timeout message during shutdown
bugs.description: The 5-minute save timeout logs a warning but continues cleanup anyway. The total shutdown sequence (including model unload and analytics) can take 10+ minutes, so the timeout message is misleading. Users may think save completed when it actually timed out.
bugs.fix: Update the timeout message to indicate actual behavior, or make the timeout truly fail the save and report to the user

bugs.name: Rust snippet slicing is not UTF-8 safe
bugs.description: get_match_context() in transcript.rs slices by byte index via &transcript[start_index..end_index]. The find() returns a byte offset on the lowercased string while slicing the original. If the transcript contains multi-byte characters (accented names, emoji, non-English text), this will panic at runtime with 'byte index is not a char boundary'.
bugs.fix: Use char_indices() or snap start_index/end_index to the nearest char boundary before slicing. E.g. while !transcript.is_char_boundary(start_index) { start_index += 1; }

bugs.name: Add FTS5 full-text search index for transcripts
bugs.description: Search uses WHERE LOWER(t.transcript) LIKE '%query%' which forces a full table scan on every query. As meetings accumulate this gets progressively slower. SQLite has built-in FTS5 support that would make searches near-instant regardless of data volume.
bugs.fix: Create a virtual table 'CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE transcripts_fts USING fts5(transcript, content=transcripts, content_rowid=rowid)' with triggers to keep it in sync. Replace LIKE query with FTS5 MATCH query.

bugs.name: Dead Python search_transcripts code with duplicated snippet logic
bugs.description: backend/app/db.py search_transcripts() (line 769) and the /search-transcripts endpoint in main.py (line 642) are dead code — the frontend calls the Rust Tauri command api_search_transcripts instead. Within the Python code, the snippet extraction logic is also copy-pasted between the transcripts loop (lines 809-822) and transcript_chunks loop (lines 836-848).
bugs.fix: Delete the Python search endpoint and DB method if confirmed unused. If kept, extract the duplicated snippet extraction into a helper function.

bugs.name: 855-line Sidebar monolith component needs decomposition
bugs.description: frontend/src/components/Sidebar/index.tsx is 855 lines doing too much: search, navigation, item rendering, modals, collapsed state, recording controls, theme toggle, logos. The renderItem function alone is ~100 lines of deeply nested JSX. This makes the component hard to maintain and test.
bugs.fix: Extract into focused components: SidebarItem (~100 lines), SearchBar (~30 lines), CollapsedSidebar (~50 lines, currently lines 476-527). Move search logic into a useSearch hook.

bugs.name: RAF not cancelled on unmount in ConversationView
bugs.description: The requestAnimationFrame call in the auto-scroll useEffect has no cleanup function. If the component unmounts while a RAF is pending, it will still execute and attempt to scroll a non-existent DOM node.
bugs.fix: Return cancelAnimationFrame(rafId) from the useEffect cleanup

bugs.name: Async setup race in OnboardingContext
bugs.description: loadOnboardingStatus() and checkDatabaseStatus() are called in useEffect without awaiting them. If the component unmounts before these async operations complete, setState will be called on an unmounted component.
bugs.fix: Wrap in async IIFE with a cancelled flag checked after each await

bugs.name: Blob URL leak on abort in ScreenshotContext
bugs.description: If the setup completes and assigns a blobUrl but the component unmounts before cleanup runs, the blob URL is never revoked. A race exists between blob URL creation and the abort check.
bugs.fix: Ensure blob URLs are always revoked in cleanup: if (blobUrlRef.current) URL.revokeObjectURL(blobUrlRef.current)

bugs.name: Async listener race in ClipboardContext
bugs.description: The setup() function is async but not awaited. If the component unmounts before setup() completes, the listeners may still be registered but cleanup finds undefined refs, leaking event listeners.
bugs.fix: Use a mounted flag pattern: check flag after each await before registering listeners

bugs.name: API key save error silently swallowed
bugs.description: The fetch call to save the API key uses .catch(() => {}) which silently swallows errors. If the backend fails to save, the user is not notified and believes their key is saved.
bugs.fix: Show a toast warning or retry on failure instead of silently swallowing

bugs.name: get_model_config returns None causing 500 error
bugs.description: If get_model_config() returns None (no config exists), the endpoint returns None directly which FastAPI cannot serialize, causing a 500 error instead of a proper empty response.
bugs.fix: Return an empty dict {} or a 404 response when model_config is None

bugs.name: SSE CancelledError re-raised prevents cleanup
bugs.description: In _sse_generator(), asyncio.CancelledError is caught and re-raised, which causes the StreamingResponse to close without draining buffered events. Cleanup code in stream_session() may not run.
bugs.fix: Don't re-raise CancelledError; break and let the generator exit cleanly so stream_session() finally block runs

bugs.name: panelWidth not transitioned on first load
bugs.description: The marginRight style is set via inline style which bypasses CSS transition-all. Content jumps instantly when the AI panel opens instead of smoothly sliding.
bugs.fix: Add transition: 'margin-right 300ms' to the inline style object

bugs.name: SSE JSON not validated against schema
bugs.description: Parsed SSE JSON is cast to ClaudeFrontendEvent without runtime validation. If the backend sends malformed events with missing fields, the handler may crash or behave unexpectedly.
bugs.fix: Add runtime validation (e.g., Zod schema) or at minimum check required fields before processing

bugs.name: Unused threading Lock import
bugs.description: Line 13 imports Lock from threading but it is never used. The SummaryProcessor docstring claims thread-safety but no locks are applied.
bugs.fix: Remove the unused import: from threading import Lock

bugs.title: AI panel voice mode requires manual first message to initialize project context
bugs.description: Ctrl+Space voice commands do not work until user manually sends a first text message to the AI panel to initialize the project/folder context. The AI panel should auto-initialize with meeting context when recording starts, so voice mode works immediately.
bugs.fix: Auto-initialize AI session with project context when recording starts or when first voice command is received, rather than requiring a manual text message.
bugs.fix_notes: Fixed 2026-03-11: Added useEffect in ClaudeProvider that watches isRecording and auto-populates projectDir, meetingId, meetingTitle via get_meeting_folder_path and get_recording_meeting_name (with 800ms retry).

bugs.title: File location links open wrong directory (Documents instead of actual path)
bugs.description: When clicking on file location links for screenshots or AI-generated files, the system opens the Documents folder instead of the actual file location. Reported for both screenshot file locations and @code command output files.
bugs.fix: Ensure file path resolution uses the actual file path rather than a default Documents directory. Check Tauri shell.open or path resolution logic.
bugs.fix_notes: Fixed 2026-03-11: Added new open_folder Rust command that opens a directory directly (with existence check) instead of show_in_folder which selects a path in its parent. On Windows, explorer /select,{dir} opens the parent; explorer {dir} opens inside.

bugs.title: AI-generated links open inside Tandem app instead of web browser
bugs.description: When the AI assistant provides clickable links (URLs) in its responses, clicking them opens the link inside the Tandem desktop app (Tauri webview) instead of opening in the users default web browser. Links should use Tauri shell.open() API to launch in the external browser.
bugs.fix: Intercept link clicks in the AI panel markdown renderer. Use Tauri shell.open() or window.__TAURI__.shell.open() to open URLs in the default external browser instead of navigating within the webview.
bugs.fix_notes: Fixed 2026-03-11: Added MarkdownLink component to ConversationView.tsx that intercepts http(s) clicks and calls invoke('open_external_url'). Converted <a> tags in ProjectDirModal.tsx and DiagramBlock.tsx to <button> with invoke('open_external_url').

bugs.title: Ctrl+Space voice mode hotkey only works once per session
bugs.description: After successfully completing one Ctrl+Space push-to-talk voice command, subsequent Ctrl+Space presses do not activate voice mode. Likely a state cleanup issue in useVoiceCommand.ts where isListeningRef, isHotkeyListeningRef, or the React state (isListening/isHotkeyListening) are not fully reset after executeCommand completes. The keydown guard at line 105 checks !isListeningRef.current which may still be true if the previous command execution had a race condition with the grace period timer.
bugs.fix: Changed keydown guard from !isListeningRef.current to !isHotkeyListeningRef.current, and added clearTimers() at the start of each new press. isListeningRef stays true during the 8s grace period (no-text case), blocking second presses — isHotkeyListeningRef is correctly reset to false in handleKeyUp so using it as the guard allows re-activation. clearTimers() cancels any pending grace period from the previous press.

bugs.title: Whisper localWhisper transcription too slow for real-time — text only appears at end of recording
bugs.description: When using localWhisper with large-v3-q5_0 model, transcription text only appears after the recording ends, not during. The model's Real-Time Factor (RTF) on CPU is ~3-8x (takes 9-24s per 3s chunk), so chunks queue up in the serial worker (NUM_WORKERS=1) and only finish processing after recording stops. CUDA detection (hardware_detector.rs:159-163) only checks env vars (CUDA_PATH/CUDA_HOME), not whether the CUDA runtime actually works — whisper.cpp likely silently falls back to CPU. User has CUDA 12.0 installed but incomplete (missing nvcc). Additionally, there is zero timing instrumentation around whisper state.full() — no way to measure actual RTF or confirm GPU vs CPU usage. Parakeet transcription works fine in real-time for comparison.
bugs.fix: 1) Add RTF timing around state.full() in whisper_engine.rs (~line 615-624) to measure processing speed. 2) Emit slow-transcription warning event to frontend from worker.rs when RTF > 1.5. 3) Add queue depth monitoring in worker dispatcher loop. 4) Surface model-unloaded errors to frontend instead of silently skipping chunks (worker.rs:136-140). 5) Consider recommending smaller models (small, medium-q5_0) for real-time use when GPU is unavailable.

bugs.name: FFmpeg encode panics on missing binary
bugs.description: encode_audio_to_format() calls Command::new("ffmpeg") with .status().expect("FFmpeg failed"). If ffmpeg is not installed, .status() returns Err and .expect() panics, crashing the app. Should return a user-friendly error instead.
bugs.fix: Replace .expect() with proper error propagation via ? or .map_err(), and surface a clear error message to the frontend.
bugs.fix_notes: Fixed 2026-03-23: Replaced .expect() and .unwrap() with proper error propagation (?, .map_err(), .ok_or_else()). Also fixes B050 (.to_str().unwrap() on non-UTF8 paths).

bugs.name: unsafe impl Send for cpal::Stream wrappers
bugs.description: The codebase uses `unsafe impl Send` on wrapper types containing cpal::Stream, which is !Send by design (platform audio handles are thread-local). Sending these across threads can cause undefined behavior or platform API violations on macOS (CoreAudio) and Windows (WASAPI).
bugs.fix: Remove unsafe impl Send. Keep streams on the thread that created them and use channels to communicate with async tasks.
bugs.fix_notes: Fixed 2026-03-23: Restructured StreamBackend::Cpal to use a dedicated OS thread (std::thread) with channel-based lifecycle management. The cpal::Stream never crosses thread boundaries. Removed all 3 'unsafe impl Send' declarations (StreamBackend, AudioStream, AudioStreamManager).

bugs.name: SummaryPanel crashes on mismatched Summary type
bugs.description: SummaryPanel expects a specific Summary object shape but receives raw JSON string or different structure from the backend (due to double-serialization in C03). Property access on undefined fields causes runtime crash.
bugs.fix: Add runtime type guard before accessing Summary properties. Handle both string and object cases gracefully.
bugs.fix_notes: Fixed 2026-03-23: Added optional chaining guards (?.) on summaryResponse.summary section accesses (key_points, action_items, decisions, main_topics). Each section block is now conditionally rendered only when .blocks exists, preventing crashes when summary structure doesn't match expected Section type.

bugs.name: Missing transcript id column in INSERT
bugs.description: save_meeting_transcript() INSERT statement does not include the `id` column, relying on SQLite ROWID auto-assignment. If the table schema defines `id` as a non-ROWID primary key, inserts will fail. Also prevents deterministic transcript IDs for deduplication.
bugs.fix: Add explicit `id` column to the INSERT with a generated UUID, or verify the schema uses INTEGER PRIMARY KEY (ROWID alias).
bugs.fix_notes: Fixed 2026-03-23: Added explicit 'id' column to the INSERT statement in save_meeting_transcript() with a uuid4()-generated value. The transcripts table schema uses 'id TEXT PRIMARY KEY' (not a ROWID alias), so the id must be explicitly provided.

bugs.name: Unauthenticated /api/notify endpoint
bugs.description: The /api/notify POST endpoint accepts arbitrary notification payloads with no authentication. Any process on the network can push notifications to all connected SSE clients, enabling phishing or social engineering via fake system messages.
bugs.fix: Add authentication (API key or localhost-only check) to the /api/notify endpoint. Consider restricting to 127.0.0.1 origin.
bugs.fix_notes: Fixed 2026-03-23: Added localhost-only restriction to /api/notify endpoint. Uses FastAPI Request object to check request.client.host against allowed hosts (127.0.0.1, ::1, localhost). Returns 403 for non-localhost callers.

bugs.name: output_path.to_str().unwrap() panics on non-UTF8 paths
bugs.description: encode_audio_to_format() calls output_path.to_str().unwrap() which panics if the path contains non-UTF8 characters (common on Windows with certain locale settings). Should use to_string_lossy() or OsStr APIs.
bugs.fix: Replace .to_str().unwrap() with .to_string_lossy() or propagate the error with .to_str().ok_or_else(|| ...).
bugs.fix_notes: Fixed 2026-03-23: Fixed as part of B045 — replaced output_path.to_str().unwrap() with .ok_or_else() that returns a descriptive error for non-UTF8 paths.

bugs.name: normalize_v2 produces NaN on empty audio
bugs.description: normalize_v2() computes max amplitude then divides all samples by it. If the input is all zeros (silence) or empty, max is 0.0 and division produces NaN, which propagates through the entire audio pipeline.
bugs.fix: Add early return for empty input and guard against zero max: if max < f32::EPSILON { return samples; }.

bugs.name: .expect() on event emit if window not ready
bugs.description: Database setup code uses app.emit("db-ready", ...).expect("Failed to emit"). If the main window is not yet created when the database initializes (race on startup), the emit fails and .expect() panics, crashing the app.
bugs.fix: Replace .expect() with .unwrap_or_else(|e| log::warn!("...")) or retry with a short delay.

bugs.name: 9+ Mutex fields with .unwrap() cause poison cascades
bugs.description: RecordingState has 9+ fields wrapped in std::sync::Mutex, all accessed with .lock().unwrap(). If any thread panics while holding one mutex, that mutex is poisoned. Subsequent .unwrap() calls on the poisoned mutex cascade the panic to every caller, making the entire recording system unrecoverable.
bugs.fix: Replace .unwrap() with .lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) to recover from poison, or use parking_lot::Mutex which does not poison.

bugs.name: cpal::Stream in tokio::sync::Mutex is not Send
bugs.description: LevelMonitor stores cpal::Stream inside a tokio::sync::Mutex. cpal::Stream is !Send on most platforms, so the tokio Mutex (which requires Send for the guarded value to work across .await points) will fail to compile or cause UB if the Send bound is bypassed via unsafe.
bugs.fix: Keep cpal::Stream on its creation thread. Use a channel (mpsc) to send level data from the audio thread to async tasks.

bugs.name: Fake sine-wave audio levels in simple_level_monitor
bugs.description: SimpleLevelMonitor generates fake audio levels using a sine wave formula instead of reading actual audio data. This produces convincing-looking but completely fabricated level meters. Likely a development stub that was never replaced.
bugs.fix: Replace sine-wave generation with actual RMS calculation from the audio capture stream, or remove SimpleLevelMonitor if LevelMonitor is the production implementation.

bugs.name: .expect() on app data dir crashes startup
bugs.description: DatabaseManager initialization calls app.path().app_data_dir().expect("Failed to get app data dir"). On sandboxed environments or unusual OS configurations where app data dir is unavailable, this panics and prevents the app from starting entirely.
bugs.fix: Replace .expect() with proper error propagation. Show a user-friendly dialog if the database directory cannot be determined.

bugs.name: 5 mutexes locked sequentially in real-time audio callback
bugs.description: The audio pipeline callback locks 5 mutexes sequentially in the hot path (audio data processing). Each lock acquisition can block if another thread holds the mutex. In a real-time audio callback, any blocking causes audio glitches (pops, dropouts). Combined with potential deadlock if lock ordering is inconsistent.
bugs.fix: Use lock-free ring buffers for audio data passing. Move mutex-guarded operations to a separate processing thread that communicates with the callback via lock-free channels.

bugs.name: title undefined in MermaidBlock handleOpenInBrowser
bugs.description: handleOpenInBrowser() uses `title` variable which may be undefined when the diagram has no explicit title. The undefined value gets interpolated into the HTML template, producing 'undefined' in the browser tab title.
bugs.fix: Add fallback: const diagramTitle = title || 'Mermaid Diagram'.

bugs.name: Stale isMonitoring closure in DeviceSelection cleanup
bugs.description: The cleanup function in the device monitoring useEffect captures `isMonitoring` from the initial render. When the effect re-runs, the cleanup still sees the old value and may skip stopping the monitor, causing leaked audio streams.
bugs.fix: Use a ref (isMonitoringRef) to track current state, and read from the ref in the cleanup function.

bugs.name: Stale models closure in WhisperModelManager listener
bugs.description: The Tauri event listener for model download progress captures the `models` array from the render when the listener was created. When a download completes and updates the model status, the listener merges the update into a stale copy, potentially reverting other model status changes.
bugs.fix: Use functional state update: setModels(prev => prev.map(m => m.name === updated.name ? {...m, ...updated} : m)).

bugs.name: AnalyticsProvider beforeunload listener cleanup leaked
bugs.description: AnalyticsProvider adds a 'beforeunload' event listener in useEffect but the cleanup function does not remove it. On hot module reload (development) or component remount, duplicate listeners accumulate, each flushing analytics on unload.
bugs.fix: Store the listener function in a variable and return () => window.removeEventListener('beforeunload', listener) from the useEffect.

bugs.name: OnboardingFlow step 4 empty on non-Mac, onComplete never called
bugs.description: Step 4 of OnboardingFlow shows macOS-specific system audio setup (BlackHole). On Windows/Linux, this step renders empty content with no way to advance. The onComplete callback is only triggered by the final step's button, so onboarding never finishes on non-Mac platforms.
bugs.fix: Skip step 4 on non-macOS platforms, or show platform-appropriate content (WASAPI loopback instructions for Windows, PulseAudio for Linux).

bugs.name: SummaryPanel fixed overlay blocks all content
bugs.description: SummaryPanel uses `fixed inset-0` positioning which creates a full-screen overlay. When the summary panel is open, it blocks interaction with all other UI elements including the sidebar and recording controls. Should use a contained layout instead.
bugs.fix: Replace `fixed inset-0` with a contained layout (e.g., flex child with overflow-auto) or add a proper dismiss mechanism with z-index management.

bugs.name: Hardcoded BACKEND URL in taskExtractionService
bugs.description: taskExtractionService.ts hardcodes 'http://localhost:5167' as the backend URL. If the backend runs on a different port or host (Docker, remote), task extraction silently fails. Should use the configurable backend URL from ConfigContext.
bugs.fix: Accept backendUrl as a parameter or import from a shared config module that reads from ConfigContext/environment.

bugs.name: YAML escape missing carriage return, tab, and control chars
bugs.description: The YAML escaping function in handoffExport.ts only escapes newlines and quotes. Carriage returns (\r), tabs (\t), and other control characters pass through unescaped, producing invalid YAML that breaks parsers.
bugs.fix: Extend escaping to handle \r, \t, \0, and all ASCII control characters (0x00-0x1F). Consider using a YAML library instead of manual escaping.

bugs.name: Forward slash path separator on Windows in claudeMdInjector
bugs.description: claudeMdInjector.ts constructs file paths using forward slashes ('/') which works in Node.js but fails when passed to Tauri Rust commands that expect platform-native separators on Windows (backslash).
bugs.fix: Use Tauri's path APIs (path.sep or path.join equivalent) to construct platform-appropriate paths.

bugs.name: Device name includes type suffix, backend cannot match
bugs.description: DeviceSelection appends ' (Microphone)' or ' (Speaker)' suffix to device names before sending to the backend. The Rust audio layer expects raw device names from cpal, so the suffixed names don't match any available device, causing silent recording failure.
bugs.fix: Strip the type suffix before sending device names to the Rust backend, or store raw name separately from display name.

bugs.name: update_meeting_name() has no transaction
bugs.description: update_meeting_name() executes a bare UPDATE without a transaction. If the app crashes mid-write, the database can be left in an inconsistent state. All multi-step database operations should use explicit transactions.
bugs.fix: Wrap the UPDATE in an async with conn.execute('BEGIN') ... conn.commit() block, or use aiosqlite's transaction context manager.

bugs.name: save_meeting() blocks on title collision via OR title=?
bugs.description: save_meeting() uses INSERT OR REPLACE with a WHERE clause that matches on `id OR title`. If two different meetings have the same title, the second INSERT silently replaces the first, losing all its data (transcripts, summaries).
bugs.fix: Remove the OR title=? condition. Match only on id for upsert. Add a unique constraint on (id) only, not title.

bugs.name: save_meeting_transcript() has no transaction
bugs.description: save_meeting_transcript() performs INSERT without a transaction wrapper. Same risk as B068 — partial writes on crash.
bugs.fix: Wrap in a transaction. Consider batching multiple transcript segments in a single transaction for performance.

bugs.name: Predictable meeting IDs from timestamp
bugs.description: Meeting IDs are generated from the current timestamp (e.g., meeting_1710000000). This is predictable and enumerable — an attacker can guess valid meeting IDs and access other users' meetings via the API (no auth required).
bugs.fix: Use uuid4() for meeting IDs. Add authentication to meeting endpoints.

bugs.name: NotificationBus publish race on _subscribers list
bugs.description: NotificationBus.publish() iterates over _subscribers while subscribe()/unsubscribe() can modify the list concurrently from different async tasks. This can cause RuntimeError: list changed during iteration.
bugs.fix: Use asyncio.Lock to protect _subscribers, or iterate over a snapshot: for sub in list(self._subscribers).

bugs.name: Synchronous Anthropic client blocks event loop
bugs.description: task_extractor.py creates a synchronous anthropic.Anthropic() client and calls client.messages.create() which blocks the async event loop. This freezes all other request handling for the duration of the API call (potentially seconds).
bugs.fix: Use anthropic.AsyncAnthropic() with await client.messages.create(), or run the sync client in a thread pool via asyncio.to_thread().

bugs.name: No file size limit on document upload
bugs.description: The document upload endpoint accepts files of any size with no limit. A malicious or accidental multi-GB upload will exhaust server memory (FastAPI reads the entire file into memory).
bugs.fix: Add Content-Length check and reject files over a reasonable limit (e.g., 50MB). Use streaming upload for larger files.

bugs.name: pd.read_csv() with no row/column limit causes memory exhaustion
bugs.description: document_parser.py calls pd.read_csv() with no nrows or usecols limit. A CSV with millions of rows or thousands of columns will consume all available memory and crash the backend.
bugs.fix: Add nrows=10000 and usecols limit. For large files, use chunked reading with pd.read_csv(chunksize=1000).

bugs.name: get_model_config() crashes on unknown provider
bugs.description: get_model_config() accesses a provider-specific config dict with a key from user input. If the provider name is not in the dict, it raises KeyError with a 500 Internal Server Error instead of a proper 400 response.
bugs.fix: Add provider validation: if provider not in SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS: raise HTTPException(400, 'Unknown provider').

bugs.name: get_transcript_config() crashes on unknown provider
bugs.description: Same issue as B076 but in the transcript configuration endpoint. Unknown provider key causes KeyError/500.
bugs.fix: Add provider validation with proper 400 error response.

bugs.name: anonymize_texts() blocks event loop with CPU-bound spaCy NER
bugs.description: anonymize_texts() runs spaCy NER inference synchronously in the async request handler. spaCy NER is CPU-intensive (100-500ms per text). During this time, the entire FastAPI event loop is blocked — no other requests can be served.
bugs.fix: Run NER in a thread pool: result = await asyncio.to_thread(analyzer.analyze, text, ...). Or use a ProcessPoolExecutor for true parallelism.

bugs.name: detail=str(e) leaks internal info in 20+ error handlers
bugs.description: Throughout main.py, exception handlers use HTTPException(500, detail=str(e)) which exposes internal error messages (file paths, SQL queries, stack traces) to API clients. This aids attackers in mapping the system.
bugs.fix: Log the full error server-side, return a generic message to clients: HTTPException(500, detail='Internal server error'). Use unique error IDs to correlate client reports with server logs.

bugs.name: ~30 .unwrap() on poisonable mutex in analytics commands
bugs.description: analytics/commands.rs has ~30 instances of .lock().unwrap() on std::sync::Mutex. If any panic occurs while a lock is held, all subsequent access panics. Low severity because analytics is non-critical functionality.
bugs.fix: Replace .unwrap() with .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) or switch to parking_lot::Mutex.

bugs.name: ~20 .unwrap() on poisonable mutex in parakeet commands
bugs.description: parakeet_engine/commands.rs has ~20 instances of .lock().unwrap(). Same poison cascade risk as B080, but for the Parakeet transcription engine.
bugs.fix: Replace .unwrap() with poison recovery or parking_lot::Mutex.

bugs.name: next_interval dead code in device_monitor
bugs.description: The `next_interval` variable is computed but never used — the monitoring loop always uses a fixed interval. Dead code that adds confusion.
bugs.fix: Remove the dead `next_interval` variable and associated computation.

bugs.name: detect_memory_gb() returns hardcoded 8GB
bugs.description: detect_memory_gb() always returns 8 as a fallback instead of actually detecting system memory. This affects model size recommendations — a 64GB machine gets the same suggestion as an 8GB machine.
bugs.fix: Use sysinfo crate or platform APIs to detect actual RAM. Keep 8GB as fallback only if detection fails.

bugs.name: Download cancel tracks only one model at a time
bugs.description: The model download cancellation mechanism uses a single AtomicBool flag. If two models are downloading simultaneously, cancelling one cancels both. Only the last-started download can be individually cancelled.
bugs.fix: Use a HashMap<ModelName, CancellationToken> to track per-model cancellation.

bugs.name: Timeout error message says 60s but actual timeout is 300s
bugs.description: The error message on LLM request timeout states '60 seconds' but the actual timeout configured is 300 seconds (5 minutes). Misleading for debugging.
bugs.fix: Update the error message to reflect the actual timeout value, or use a constant for both.

bugs.name: manager_for_cleanup variable shadowing
bugs.description: In stop_recording(), `manager_for_cleanup` is created by taking the value out of RECORDING_MANAGER, but a later block shadows it with a new binding of the same name. The original value is dropped prematurely, potentially skipping cleanup steps.
bugs.fix: Rename one of the bindings to avoid shadowing, or restructure to use a single binding throughout.

bugs.name: Recording chunk ID differs from source chunk ID
bugs.description: When the pipeline sends audio chunks to the recording saver, it generates a new chunk ID instead of using the source chunk's ID. This breaks the ability to correlate recorded chunks with their transcription results.
bugs.fix: Pass through the original chunk_id from the source AudioChunk to the recording saver.

bugs.name: .expect() on app data dir in parakeet init
bugs.description: Parakeet engine initialization calls app.path().app_data_dir().expect() which panics if the directory is unavailable. Same issue as B056 but in the Parakeet module.
bugs.fix: Replace .expect() with error propagation via ? operator.

bugs.name: SystemTime::now() panics if system clock is before Unix epoch
bugs.description: stt.rs uses SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap() which panics if the system clock is set before 1970-01-01. Unlikely but possible on embedded or misconfigured systems.
bugs.fix: Use .unwrap_or_default() or handle the error case.

bugs.name: .expect() on hardcoded model list parse
bugs.description: Model list parsing uses .expect() on a hardcoded JSON string. Since the input is compile-time constant, this can only fail if the code is modified incorrectly. Very low risk but technically a panic point.
bugs.fix: Use a compile-time validated constant or include_str! with a test to catch parse failures at build time.

bugs.name: try_lock silently drops audio level data
bugs.description: LevelMonitor uses try_lock() in the audio callback. If the lock is contended, the audio level data for that callback is silently dropped. Over time, this causes the level meter to appear choppy or unresponsive.
bugs.fix: Use a lock-free atomic (AtomicF32 or AtomicU32 with f32 bit casting) for the level value, or an mpsc channel.

bugs.name: mermaidInitialized flag never resets on theme change
bugs.description: MermaidBlock uses a module-level `mermaidInitialized` flag that is set once and never reset. When the theme changes (light/dark), mermaid.initialize() should be called again with new theme config, but the flag prevents re-initialization.
bugs.fix: Reset mermaidInitialized when theme changes, or make initialization theme-aware by comparing current theme to last-initialized theme.

bugs.name: Blob URL not revoked in fallback render path
bugs.description: MermaidBlock creates blob URLs for SVG rendering. The primary path revokes the URL after use, but the fallback error-recovery path creates a new blob URL without revoking it, causing a memory leak per failed render.
bugs.fix: Add URL.revokeObjectURL() in the fallback path's cleanup, or use a useEffect cleanup to revoke all created URLs.

bugs.name: fetchDevices not wrapped in useCallback
bugs.description: fetchDevices() is defined as a plain function inside the component. It is used as a dependency in useEffect but recreated every render, causing the effect to re-run unnecessarily and re-fetch the device list.
bugs.fix: Wrap fetchDevices in useCallback with appropriate dependencies.

bugs.name: Unnecessary deps in initializeModels effect
bugs.description: The useEffect that initializes model list includes unnecessary dependencies that cause it to re-run and re-fetch the model list when unrelated state changes.
bugs.fix: Review and minimize the dependency array to only include values that should trigger re-initialization.

bugs.name: initialized ref reset is dead code in AnalyticsProvider
bugs.description: The cleanup function sets initialized.current = false, but since the provider is mounted at the app root and never unmounts, this code never executes. If it did execute (e.g., during HMR), it would cause double initialization.
bugs.fix: Remove the dead reset or add a guard against double initialization.

bugs.name: RegExp compiled on every render per segment
bugs.description: TranscriptView creates a new RegExp object for search highlighting on every render, for every transcript segment. With 100+ segments and frequent re-renders during recording, this creates thousands of unnecessary RegExp compilations.
bugs.fix: Memoize the RegExp with useMemo, keyed on the search query string.

bugs.name: Streaming interval cleanup race in TranscriptView
bugs.description: TranscriptView uses setInterval for streaming text animation. The cleanup in useEffect may not fire if the component unmounts during the interval callback, leaving an orphaned interval that tries to update unmounted state.
bugs.fix: Add a mounted ref check inside the interval callback, and ensure clearInterval is called in all cleanup paths.

bugs.name: waitForInitialization busy-waits with polling
bugs.description: analytics.ts waitForInitialization() polls a boolean flag every 100ms using setInterval. This wastes CPU and delays readiness detection by up to 100ms. Should use a Promise/callback pattern instead.
bugs.fix: Replace polling with a Promise that resolves when initialization completes. Use a resolve callback stored in a module-level variable.

bugs.name: Failed analytics init allows repeated re-init attempts
bugs.description: If analytics initialization fails, the initialized flag remains false, allowing every subsequent call to retry initialization. This can cause repeated failed network requests or error spam in the console.
bugs.fix: Add an initFailed flag to prevent retry after failure, or implement exponential backoff for retries.

bugs.name: onCancel missing from effect dependency array
bugs.description: RegionSelectOverlay's Escape key handler uses onCancel callback but it is not in the useEffect dependency array. If onCancel changes (e.g., parent re-renders with new callback), the old callback is invoked.
bugs.fix: Add onCancel to the dependency array, or use a ref to always call the latest callback.

bugs.name: const declaration in switch case without block scope
bugs.description: handoffExport.ts uses const declarations inside switch cases without wrapping them in blocks. In strict mode, this can cause 'already declared' errors if cases fall through, and makes the code fragile to reordering.
bugs.fix: Add block scope to switch cases: case 'x': { const ...; break; }.

bugs.name: Voice command UI mismatches push-to-talk implementation
bugs.description: CommandSettings shows voice commands as toggle-based (click to start, click to stop) but the actual implementation uses push-to-talk (hold Ctrl+Space). The UI gives incorrect usage instructions.
bugs.fix: Update the UI to show push-to-talk instructions: 'Hold Ctrl+Space to speak, release to send'.

bugs.name: SSE reconnection timeout not cleared on unmount
bugs.description: NotificationContext sets a setTimeout for SSE reconnection on error. If the component unmounts before the timeout fires, the callback runs and tries to establish a new connection to a dead context.
bugs.fix: Store the timeout ID and clear it in the useEffect cleanup function.

bugs.name: handoffSettings stale in confirm callback
bugs.description: useHandoffExport's confirm callback captures handoffSettings from the closure at creation time. If settings change between dialog open and confirm click, the stale settings are used for the export.
bugs.fix: Use a ref for handoffSettings and read from .current in the callback.

bugs.name: Edit/delete buttons not visible on keyboard focus
bugs.description: EditableTitle shows edit/delete action buttons on hover (:hover CSS), but they are not accessible via keyboard navigation. A keyboard-only user cannot access the edit or delete actions.
bugs.fix: Add :focus-within to the parent container to show action buttons when any child has keyboard focus.

bugs.name: pathSep() called repeatedly without caching
bugs.description: handoffService.ts calls pathSep() (which invokes a Tauri command) on every path construction. This makes an IPC round-trip each time. The path separator never changes during the app's lifetime.
bugs.fix: Cache the result of pathSep() in a module-level variable on first call.

bugs.name: update_meeting_title() has no transaction
bugs.description: update_meeting_title() executes a bare UPDATE without a transaction wrapper. Same class of issue as B068/B070 but lower impact since title updates are infrequent.
bugs.fix: Wrap in a transaction for consistency with other database operations.

bugs.name: Notification level field not validated
bugs.description: The /api/notify endpoint accepts any string for the notification 'level' field. Invalid levels (e.g., 'critical', 'debug') are stored and forwarded to SSE clients, which may not handle unexpected values.
bugs.fix: Validate level against allowed values: Literal['info', 'warning', 'error', 'success'] in the Pydantic model.

bugs.name: Anthropic HTTP client not closed — connection leak
bugs.description: task_extractor.py creates an Anthropic client but never calls client.close(). Each extraction request creates a new client with its own connection pool, leaking TCP connections over time.
bugs.fix: Use a module-level client singleton, or use context manager: async with anthropic.AsyncAnthropic() as client: ...

bugs.name: SQL injection via unsanitized DDL identifiers
bugs.description: schema_validator.py constructs ALTER TABLE statements by interpolating column names from the schema definition. If a column name contains SQL injection payload, it executes arbitrary SQL. Low risk because schema is defined in code, not user input.
bugs.fix: Sanitize identifiers by rejecting names that don't match [a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]* pattern, or use proper identifier quoting.

bugs.name: Entity offsets reference original text, not anonymized output
bugs.description: The anonymizer returns entity offset information (start/end positions) that reference the original un-anonymized text. After surrogate replacement (which changes string length), these offsets point to wrong positions in the anonymized output.
bugs.fix: Recalculate entity offsets after surrogate replacement, accounting for length differences between original entities and surrogates.

bugs.name: Global _registries dict mutated without lock
bugs.description: anonymizer.py uses a global _registries dict to store entity-to-surrogate mappings. Multiple concurrent requests can read and write this dict simultaneously without synchronization, causing race conditions and inconsistent surrogate assignment.
bugs.fix: Add asyncio.Lock around _registries access, or use a thread-safe dict implementation.

bugs.name: update_meeting_summary() has no transaction
bugs.description: update_meeting_summary() performs UPDATE without transaction. Same class as B068/B070/B108.
bugs.fix: Wrap in a transaction.

bugs.name: get_all_meetings() has no error handling
bugs.description: get_all_meetings() has no try/except. If the database is locked, corrupted, or the table doesn't exist, the exception propagates up to the API handler as an unhandled 500 error with full traceback in the response.
bugs.fix: Add try/except with proper error handling. Return empty list on recoverable errors, raise HTTPException with clean message on fatal errors.

bugs.name: Missing env vars silently replaced with empty string
bugs.description: claude_agent.py uses os.environ.get('VAR', '') for required environment variables like ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. If the key is missing, an empty string is passed to the Anthropic client which then fails with an unhelpful authentication error instead of a clear 'API key not configured' message.
bugs.fix: Check for empty/missing API key at startup and raise a clear ConfigurationError with instructions.

bugs.name: meeting_title not sanitized in generated Markdown
bugs.description: generate_claude_md() interpolates meeting_title directly into Markdown content. A title containing Markdown syntax (e.g., '# Drop Table', '[link](javascript:alert(1))') would alter the generated CLAUDE.md structure or inject content.
bugs.fix: Sanitize meeting_title by escaping Markdown special characters before interpolation.
